reading.text:
Reading of def PaperSpec.A.RepresentsMart (sec. 2 PRP paragraph, 02-model-assumptions.tex:47-56).

Paper notion. A square-integrable (F_t)-martingale M (R^m- or R-valued) on [0,T] is represented
by (Z,U) when
  M_t = M_0 + int_0^t Z_s dW_s + int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de)   for every t in [0,T] (a.s.),
with (Z,U) a predictable square-integrable pair: Z predictable R^{m x d} (or 1 x d) valued with
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < inf; U predictable (P (x) E-measurable, or predictable L^2(nu)-valued via
(2.3)) with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L^2(nu)} dt < inf; M_0 F_0-measurable. The stochastic integrals
are the L^2 Ito integral w.r.t. W and the compensated Poisson integral w.r.t. Ntilde = N - dt nu,
for the filtration of sec. 2.
A faithful Lean definition must contain: the predictability and square integrability of Z, U
(or these must be supplied at every use, e.g. inside an existential that includes them);
the identity at every t in [0,T] a.s. (or indistinguishability); the right integrals; no extra
constraint on M beyond what the paper has. The F_0-measurability of M_0 can be in the PRP
statement instead (it is automatic for adapted M). Junk: if the integrals take junk value 0 on
non-integrable integrands, the integrability fields are essential (otherwise any M with
M_t = M_0 + 0 would be "represented" by a non-integrable pair, making uniqueness false and
existence trivial in degenerate cases).

comparison.text:
Comparison, PaperSpec.A.RepresentsMart (Sec2Basics.lean:91-110).

- Z : R -> Omega -> Fin d -> R (row vector for scalar M): each coordinate predictable for enlJoint
  (the sec. 2 filtration), vanishing off [0,T], finite energy E int_0^T |Z^j|^2 < inf. OK (H^2_W).
- U : R -> Omega -> E -> R: MarkedPredictable for enlJoint (measurable for the sigma-algebra
  generated by F x (r,q] x B, F in F_r, r >= 0, nu(B) < inf, i.e. P (x) E on positive times), vanishing
  off [0,T], finite marked energy E int_0^T int_E |U|^2 nu(de) dt < inf. OK (H^2_N, P (x) E version).
  Note: marked-predictable plus vanishing for s < 0 forces U = 0 at s = 0 (the sigma-algebra does
  not separate points of Omega x (-inf,0] x E); a single time is dt-null, so any representing pair
  can be so normalised.
- Identity: for every t in [0,T], a.s. M_t = M_0 + sum_j int_0^t Z^j dW^j + int_0^t int_E U Ntilde -
  L^2 Ito integral and L^2 compensated Poisson integral of LevyStochCalc over enlJoint. OK.
- The integrability fields are inside the existential (hZ, hZe, hU, hUe), so no junk-value
  integral is used. M_0 F_0-measurability is not part of it (automatic for adapted M; recorded in
  the PRP statement's hypotheses via Martingale).
- Scalar M (vector case componentwise).
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: scalar martingale M (the R^m case is componentwise) and Z a d-row; Z and U
normalised to vanish off [0,T] (for U this also forces U = 0 at time 0, a dt-null time, since the
marked predictable sigma-algebra only charges positive times); U as a real P (x) E-measurable
function (the paper's reading of L^2(nu)-valued integrands through a P (x) E representative,
(2.3)); predictability, finite energy and the identity at each t in [0,T] (a.s.) as in the paper; the
L^2 stochastic integrals of LevyStochCalc over the sec. 2 filtration enlJoint.
